source.description: Project-code materialization point where the attacker-controlled value string is copied into kv->val as an SDS allocation.
source.value_from: The fuzz harness converts PoC bytes to strings and passes them into the fluent-bit kv API; this project call is the scored source boundary.; value `k_buf, v_buf`; from `return flb_kv_item_create_len(list, k_buf, k_len, v_buf, v_len);`

sink.description: Second free of kv->val during flb_kv_release(); ASan reports the underlying free through flb_sds_destroy/flb_free.

root_cause.description: For FLB_CONFIG_MAP_STR multi entries, entry->val.str is assigned kv->val by shallow copy, creating shared ownership between the config map entry and the original kv item.

tainted_value_origin.description: The attacker-controlled value becomes an allocated SDS owned by the kv item.

coarse_trace.summary: Attacker-controlled value bytes are copied into kv->val as a new SDS string.
The config map stores a shallow alias of kv->val into a multi-value string entry instead of duplicating the SDS.
Destroying the config map releases entry->val.str, which is the aliased kv->val pointer.
The original kv list is released after the config map has already freed the aliased value.
kv->val is destroyed a second time, producing the ASan double-free.

fine_trace.code: return flb_kv_item_create_len(list, k_buf, k_len, v_buf, v_len);
fine_trace.note: The harness has already derived null-terminated strings from the PoC; this project API receives those attacker-controlled strings and forwards them to the allocating helper.
The attacker-controlled property value is copied into a new SDS allocation owned by the kv item.
The property list containing the kv item is consumed by the config-map checker.
The current attacker-controlled key/value entry is selected from the property list.
The matching config-map entry is a string multi-value entry, so the vulnerable string branch is taken.
Root cause: shallow copy creates two owners of the same SDS pointer: entry->val.str in the config map and kv->val in the original property list.
The config map destroy path releases the multi-value entry, causing the first free of the aliased SDS.
ASan free_context points through this call: value->val.str is the same pointer as kv->val because of the shallow copy.
After flb_config_map_destroy(), the fuzzer releases the original property list; kv still contains the stale pointer.
Second destruction of the same SDS pointer reaches flb_free and triggers ASan double-free.
